title: Meta’s Scrapped AI-Native Plan Included 60% Team Reductions and AI Agents Causing Disruptions
summary: Meta explored a plan (Project OT) to reduce team sizes by up to 60% and replace human tasks with AI agents to become 'AI native.' The initiative, led by Mark Zuckerberg, included two rounds of layoffs but was canceled after the first round in May due to productivity concerns, technical disruptions, and employee morale issues. Internal documents revealed AI agents made 'large-scale, disruptive actions,' increased security incidents by 40%, and failed to accelerate productivity as expected.
key_points: Meta’s Project OT aimed to reduce team headcounts by up to 60% to transition the company into an 'AI-native' organization, where AI agents would handle most daily tasks.
The plan, initiated by Mark Zuckerberg, included two rounds of layoffs, but only the first (in May) was executed before the second was canceled.
Meta explored scenarios where small teams would oversee AI systems, potentially reducing headcount by 25% or more, with savings redirected to high-performing AI engineers.
Internal documents defined 'AI native' as a company with automated workflows, AI-first builds, and third-party AI agent sales (which Meta began in June).
A pilot program restructured teams into smaller groups, removing middle management and using 'agent-assisted analysis' for task prioritization.
AI agents caused significant disruptions, including a 40% increase in major technical/security incidents and a 70% rise in time spent resolving issues.
Productivity metrics showed a 220% increase in code changes but only a 36% rise in new/upgraded features reaching users, raising doubts about AI’s efficiency.
Employee morale declined due to layoff rumors and Meta’s paused program tracking keyboard/mouse input for AI training.
Zuckerberg acknowledged in July that AI agent development had not accelerated as expected, contributing to the project’s cancellation.
Meta’s case highlights the challenges and risks of overhauling workforce structures with AI, including unintended disruptions and unmet productivity goals.

reason.details: The article provides a detailed, well-sourced analysis of Meta’s Project OT, including internal documents, productivity metrics, and leadership statements. It balances factual reporting (e.g., layoffs, AI disruptions, security incidents) with contextual insights (e.g., employee morale, Zuckerberg’s acknowledgment of unmet goals). The content is relevant to the AI category, avoids sensationalism, and distinguishes between reported facts and implications. No evidence of spam, clickbait, or disguised advertising. Minor deductions in score for lack of direct employee quotes, but overall highly informative and objective.
